a.text: Let someone better take over? Haha, if Father heard that, I'm sure he'd be chewing your head off.
Don't joke with me, Brother. Of all us siblings, who could compare to you in either knowledge or strength?

Once you ascend the throne and move into the Forbidden City, I can leave for the Sky Mirror Pavilion with peace of mind. I'll set up shop as a scribe and look after all Yan's ancient records. In a way, I'll also take some weight off your shoulders.
Brother, no more hesitating! At this point, only you can... convince Father.
The Grand Preceptor... no, all three Grand Ministers support this move! Even in the face of the officers, of Yan's citizens, public opinion will still bear out.
Brother, this is the right thing to do! You can't pull out now!
Why me? Why did it have to be me?!
Our youngest brother died because of you! They all died because of you!
You shove it all on me, make me take the blame alone, deal with the whole warring mess alone, and you just leave like nothing happened?!

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Look how idle you are. All the Mid-Autumn festivities of Lungmen, and you don't plan to attend a single one?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Should I? Who wants to see my wrinkly mug on their TV, anyway?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: The Schwires' girl is a planner. She'll handle it. She can make anything lively.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: I've watched you grow lazier day after day since we came back from Yumen. You just coop up in your study at home eating snacks. If you don't go out for a walk any time soon, you might just start putting on a beer belly.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hah hah... I haven't seen Lin Kojui get out much since spring. I can't even find a partner for morning jogs now.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Ah... he's old, I'm old, the young ones know how to do it all. If I keep sticking my head in, they won't think I'm cool.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: So now you understand, huh? If you'd realized any sooner, would little Ch'en have ever left?

spans.text: you understand, huh? If you'd realized any sooner, would little Ch'en have ever left?

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: How long ago was it?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Sorry, what?

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Little Ch'en. How long has it been since she left?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Five years.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: It's been five years.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: We don't even know what she's going through out there, or how her disease is.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I know she was at Yumen, when I was there.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: She's doing fine. Her swordsmanship's progressed... so she's fine, I suppose.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: So you just watched her leave again?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: She doesn't want to see me, and she doesn't want to come back. I can't force her.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Don't worry. Her path's longer than ours.

steps.name: Shadow Guard
steps.text: Lord Wei, a letter to you.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...That they made you deliver personally...

steps.name: Shadow Guard
steps.text: It's from the capital.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: The sender...?

steps.name: Shadow Guard
steps.text: His Majesty's Imperial Guard.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Did he have any message aside from the letter?

steps.name: Shadow Guard
steps.text: The True Lung invites Lord Wei to the capital for the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies, and for a moon-viewing together.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Leave the letter on my desk. You're dismissed for now.

steps.name: Shadow Guard
steps.text: If we may ask what Lord Wei intends.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I have my own plans. None of you need to worry.

steps.name: Shadow Guard
steps.text: Lord Wei, we volunteer to escort you to the capital!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...I said you're dismissed!

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Why don't we open up your invitation and see what they wrote exactly?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: No need. Just leave it there.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: This day was meant to come. I even thought it'd come a little sooner.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: ...How many years has it been?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Forty... it's been forty whole years since I left Baizao.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Yumen should've reached the capital by now. I suppose my brother's settling all his old debts in one clean go.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: A clean slate in time for autumn... A fine autumn at that.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: You can choose not to go.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: It's been forty years already, what's he going to do? Send another unit of Imperial Guards, a whole army—

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...Enough nonsense!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: At this point, that's not what he intends...

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Then what does he intend?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You know, I've never really brought up those days with him before...

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Enough. I don't want to hear it.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Fumizuki, I've let down a lot of people throughout my life...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Edward, my sister, my teacher...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: And I have to admit that my brother's turned out to be one more on the pile.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: You can also say that it was the position that killed so many people.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...And who had a choice?

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Then it wasn't your fault.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Even if you'd stayed, would things have turned out better? Would there be no blood?

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Nobody would have remembered a minister pleading the commoners' case. They would only remember a regicidal, fratricidal prince!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If you have questions, ask. I'm in a hurry.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Mind your attitude. You're also a theoretical suspect in our crime scene. But seeing as you're a coworker, I'll spare you the interrogation room.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I told you! I saw the culprit on the scene, I just miscalculated and failed to arrest him—

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Calm down. Are you going to physically vent on me just because you didn't catch the one who did it?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...I'd have to match your strength first.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Good. You're still somewhat sober.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: In light of the years we've spent together in the Judicial, then, can you tell me—

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: This afternoon, why were you at Ding Feng Lou, at the scene of the crime?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...An investigation.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: In the runup to the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies, we've had the scrollery be burned, then two fires at Ding Feng Lou. Don't you think this string of cases could be connected somehow?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: So you're saying you knew beforehand that someone would set fire to Ding Feng Lou today, and thus you were lying in wait for them?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I was just there following up a lead...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: 'Just' there following up a lead... Do you need me to list off every action you've taken the last few days?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You've been tailing me?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: I don't have that sort of free time... but I have ways of knowing these things, naturally.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Let me ask once more. Who were you meeting at Ding Feng Lou today?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...I fear I'm not the only one working on the sly.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Explain?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: For your information, you never told me the Ministry of Rites' files on Gu Quan were forged, and that he was sent to death row before leaving Baizao... As a minister, you must have known these things.

spans.text: For your information, you never told me the Ministry of Rites' files on Gu Quan were forged, and that he was sent to death row before leaving Baizao... As a minister,
you must have known these things.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: These are all clearly key points of evidence. Why were they nowhere to be found in the Judicial Review Office archives? And why would you cover up—

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: So this is the lead on the scrollery fire that you've been toiling over for the last few days...? How did you find any of this out?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: It's none of your concern how I found out...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: There is a piece of advice I gave to Yu Cheng in the past, and I will give it to you now.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Some past affairs are learned of. Some are not learned of. In both cases, there are reasons why.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Some things are best left forgotten by all.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I never imagined I'd hear those words come from a minister.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You may consider me a schemer all you like, a minister merely booted over from the Ministry of Justice.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: But I know exactly what I'm saying.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: And I know that regardless of the thousands of reasons you might have, the truth is still and merely the truth, not anyone's tool to broaden the divide.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: There will always be someone who remembers the truth, and the meaning behind it.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: For example, that girl shut in the next room—whom you took every pain to secretly bring back to Baizao all the way from Victoria?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yes... I did uncover that Gu Quan had a daughter in Victoria. She too can provide vital testimony in the Gu Quan case—

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Lin Qingyan, when will you stop playing dumb?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You've already found out that the Gu Quan files are fake. You know Yu Cheng is on the trail of that very case...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: So I'm guessing you've also found out about the child who the Imperial Guard brought back forty years ago, who they recorded in the files as deceased... You have your suspicions as to the truth of this case, correct?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Was that girl you brought back here born in Victoria, or born in Baizao?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You know full well.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You clearly long suspected her identity, and still, you decided to bring her back. Were you that confident you could pull this off without a hitch...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Or was it that in pursuit of the 'truth', you didn't even care if she lived or died?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You're threatening me...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You think I'm joking?
Lin Qingyan's gaze fixes tight on the minister's notes. She doesn't even notice how her own attire is soaked through in cold sweat.
But in the next instant, with a bizarre warping of light, the paper in her hands vanishes.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: But back on topic, that's not what I care about. At least, right now, it's not what I care about most.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: I've told you, past affairs are never as important as present.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: So what are these present affairs of yours?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You know that Yumen is less than a hundred li from Baizao right now. For three months, Baizao has been preparing to split up and move.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...And how does this relate to the Gu Quan case?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Should you keep investigating this case, then there will only be one person in all of Yan who can give you your answers.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Qingyan, take one step out of this door, and I can no longer protect you.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: ...Let alone her.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: At the Ch'ens' old place, in the study, there's a secret closet. After I leave, go there, and take what's inside.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Follow those instructions, and you can protect Lungmen's safety, and your own.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: So you're going?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Now's the perfect time to. Kojui's girl is doing a great job handling the downtown, and the Schwires' future doesn't rest on the sick old tiger anymore.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Lungmen doesn't need a Wei Yenwu anymore, or a Chief Executive...

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: I think you're giving your last words a little too early.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: This is about Lungmen's future... Fumizuki, listen to me...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I've made a lot of mistakes, done a lot of things I regret... but Lungmen, our city, built by us... a home to millions—

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Lungmen must stay.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Then you stay too, and take care of it.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Youngsters can handle it all, but it still needs some oldies to look after it.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You see this letter too. How am I meant to ignore this?

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: So once again you'll just roll over and die? Just like last time you'd pay with your life, is that how you're envisioning it? Does that make anything even?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...It's different this time!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: There's no one standing on the other side, I'm just facing my own debts.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I made a choice forty years ago... and ever since, with every action I take, I try to convince myself—that even knowing how many people I've failed, I was still right to make that choice.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: But I can't run forever.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: You know, your life's never been yours alone. Not then, and certainly not now.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Forget about sacrificing yourself to make up for anything. You can't make up for a mistake with another mistake—it never ends that way. At our age, we should've already learned that lesson well.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Stay. We'll face this together.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Fumizuki... Don't try and stop me!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You cannot stop me... paying for my past.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Well then, you leave me with no other choice.

spans.text: you leave me with no other choice.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: While I'm stood here, you're not going anywhere.

steps.name: Fumizuki
steps.text: Yenwu, this time, I'll protect you. I swear it.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Leizi!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You're... you're alright?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Of course I'm alright!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: All that Judicial lady asked was what I saw during the fire, and I just told the truth—I didn't see anything! So then she let me go.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: The heck did you do? How come you took so long?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: It's no matter now. Let's go.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Wait, wait, wait! Go? Why?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: That Mo Bufu clearly still has tons of answers! Aren't we gonna follow up with him?!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: There's nothing to follow up on.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Pardon?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I'm not meddling with your father's case anymore.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I'll get you out of Baizao in the next day or two.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Lin Qingyan! That's one stupid joke to tell me now, you know that?!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: No, wait... you just found a new lead, didn't you? That's why you're just screwing with me?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Okay now, for real, tell me what you found or—

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Blaze!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I got the official debriefing from the Judicial case files.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Gu Quan... an ethnic Yanese from Victoria, joined the Ministry of Rites in 1077 as a ceremonial officer.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Reassigned as envoy of ceremonial rites in 1092, headed for Victoria as part of a diplomatic mission. On the way, encountered an unexpected snowstorm, and passed away after falling into a river.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Leizi... you're lying to me, aren't you...? Just trying to shove me out of the picture again?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You've been asking me just what the deal was with your father's death, haven't you?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Well, every lead's been thoroughly investigated. There's no doubt. That's it, it was just an accident...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: All the gaps in the files have been made replete.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...This case can be closed.
In creeps the mid-autumn. The night sky is moonless.
Out in the streets, the energy poles churn away at max output, but the drop in temperature is still noticeable to some.
All falls still in the dead of night. The human sea recedes. The biting breeze blows through.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Achoo—!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: If you're that cold, just turn on the heater.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Easy for you to say. If we're going to keep running this shabby little eatery, we have to pinch every penny we can on warmth...

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Dammit, look how late it is. When will Blaze and her friend show up?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You're wondering about that reward money, huh...

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: A... Am not! Achoo—!

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Is this window letting air in? I need to fix it later—

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Wait, are they back...?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: You... You're—

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: What? Am I not allowed in?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: P-Please, come inside, I'll put on some tea for you now... Anything to eat?

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Noodles. Longevity noodles.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: R... Right, I'll make you some now!

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Ones made by your boss.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: W-Well...
Jiang glances back at the staircase where the Young Chef had been standing; by now he's vanished without a trace.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Er... he's out on business.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Then I'll wait for him here.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Far, far out... he won't be back for a fortnight.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: And I'll still wait.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: I've waited thirty years. So long that I'm shriveled up. What's a little longer?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Chef Mo, please don't joke around now...

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: You're the first under heaven when it comes to cooking. What could be worth wasting your time here?

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Ma de... First under whose heaven?!
Mo Bufu downs his teacup in one go.
The hot tea spills from the corners of his mouth, and drips down his wizened white beard.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: I remember clearly... that winter thirty years ago, a Catastrophe wrecked my home village. Those of us lucky enough to survive took off, me with nothing but my cooking skills. We thought, let's scrape by in Baizao.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: We went through hell. We were almost there when we ran into another group of refugees—or maybe a bandit gang, I'm not sure.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: They followed us for a long way across that icy waste, weapons in hand. We began to realize that they were after the remaining supplies and rations we had left.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: By the time we'd been trekking for a month, plenty of us were sick or hurt. We had barely scraps left to eat, far from enough for both sides to cross that wasteland.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: There was no escape, so we decided we may as well risk it all with them. However, when we were just about to go out fighting, we smelt something delicious. That's when we saw him...

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: There was an old temple not far away from where we were. Someone'd set up a stove by the gateway, boiling up a wok of noodles. We couldn't see his face properly, through all the steam.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: We had no clue why someone would be making noodles there, but we were past the point of wondering, of asking, even of fighting.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: That wonderful smell and those piping hot noodles drew all of us near the wok, and we waited around him quietly.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Never before had I eaten something so delicious...

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: The moment those noodles entered my mouth, I felt like my tongue had been numb for decades, only to spring back to life right then and there.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: All along, I never knew that a meal could taste so arresting, so absorbing.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: It felt like a flavor beyond us humans...

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: By the time I finished my noodles and looked up from my bowl, he was gone.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Who knew that in my lifetime studying as a cook, the most profound lesson I'd learn would be in a shack of a temple outside Baizao City.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: From then on, I apprenticed all over, so that one day, I might make a bowl of noodles like those.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: But I couldn't... In the end, I just can't.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: You know, what if you're misremembering... I mean, look, you were starving at the time, maybe that's why you found that bowl of noodles so tasty—

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Do you not trust my tongue?

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Thirty years a bowl of noodles has been burned into my mind. Thirty years I've been searching for it.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: If whoever that was is still in Baizao, he must be over fifty by now...

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: I searched all over this city. The well-known tea maker in the north, nothing. The guy who made the best pastries in the south, still nothing...

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: I searched and searched, until my fellow oldies in cooking retired, and only I was left. I was on the verge of giving up...

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: But today, once more, I tasted it...

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: I don't know why... her cooking skills were immature, but the noodles she brought forth tasted exactly like it.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: It was your chef here who taught her those noodles, am I right?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: How do you know...

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: We sent out a hundred written invitations for the Ding Feng Lou competition. I can recall every one. I've long been aware your Savors at Yu's had a reputation.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: I don't know what kind of relation your chef and that savior of mine have, and I have no clue why he's willing to waste his talents away like this.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: But I won't do the same... All the cooking skills I've inherited over the years, I can't let them end with me.
Mo Bufu stands, produces a letter from his pocket, and places it on the table.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: ...You tell him this. That untrained disciple of his? She passes.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Tell her to report to Ding Feng Lou two days later before noon.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Huh...? She just—passes?

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: You get good enough business here. Did this doorstep sink again recently?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: We haven't replaced it in over ten years.

steps.name: Mo Bufu
steps.text: Low doorsteps can't keep the wind out. It's getting colder in the coming days.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: The boss won't let me. He says the lower, the better. Too high and all the diners will stop coming.
Mo Bufu steps over that low, low doorstep, and disappears into the thick of night.
Once again, the restaurant is empty save for squalls of wind through the hall. Their whistle grows louder, as if lamenting.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: ...Is he gone?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: *Sigh*... You really are—*Sigh*!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I heard Blaze passed the test? Does that mean the prize money—

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Forget about the prize money!

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: What's wrong with you to torment a man like that... He's seventy, eighty years old, and you'll just watch him freak out like that?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: He just can't find an apprentice to fit him, right? What's to worry about... Look at me, I never worry about things like that.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Put yourself in his shoes, he's spent a lifetime honing his craft, just for it to be lost in a blink—

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Well, if it's lost, it's lost.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Ai—!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: It's his future reputation he cares about right now, it's the title of 'first under heaven' he's carrying, it's others' cuisine he's obsessed with—there's no way he can focus on his own craft and improve it at this rate.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: If he can't make it through this, nobody can help him.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Aiyo, Blaze's back.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Look how late it is, I bet you haven't eaten? I'll go make you something now.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Congrats! I've got good news for you, you passed the Ding Feng Lou exam.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: We'll split the reward money thirty-seventy like we agreed—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You don't care?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: If you're that good for money, how about leaving your thirty percent of—

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Huh? Xingzhu didn't come back with you?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Right, where's Xingzhu?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Oh, she dropped in this afternoon while Jiang was out buying ingredients. She left you a note too.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Left me a note...?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You have passed the Ding Feng Lou Chef Selection. Please fol—

steps.name: Young Chef
